claim: Rider is a cross-platform .NET IDE running on Windows, macOS and Linux and is free for non-commercial use.
quote: JetBrains Rider is a truly cross-platform IDE, providing a seamless development experience across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

claim: The free non-commercial Rider subscription runs one year, auto-renews only if used in the last 6 months, may not be used for commercial projects, and enables detailed code-related data collection by default.
quote: Non-commercial subscriptions are issued for one year and will automatically renew after that, however, for the renewal to happen, you must have used the assigned license at least once during the last 6 months of the subscription period.

claim: Visual Studio 2026 requires 64-bit Windows 10/11 or Windows Server; there is no Linux or macOS build.
quote: Visual Studio 2026 supports Windows 10 and Windows 11 on x64 hardware, along with Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025.

claim: Azure Data Studio retired on 2026-02-28; Microsoft points at VS Code + the MSSQL extension and tells you to keep SSMS for SQL Server Agent and full administration.
quote: Azure Data Studio is retired as of February 28, 2026 and no longer receives updates or security fixes. Migrate to Visual Studio Code with the MSSQL extension for continued support.

claim: SQL Server 2025 runs natively on RHEL 9/10 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, x86-64 only, with CU7 (17.0.4065.4) shipped 2026-07-16; SLES is dropped from 2025 onward.
quote: SQL Server container images are supported only on Linux hosts running on Intel and AMD x86-64 CPUs. Emulation or translation environments (for example, Rosetta 2, Prism, or QEMU) aren't tested or supported.

claim: On modern Ubuntu the Microsoft package feed no longer carries .NET; .NET 10 comes from the built-in Ubuntu feed, or from ppa:dotnet/backports on 22.04/24.04.
quote: .NET is available in the Ubuntu package manager feeds. The Microsoft package repository no longer contains .NET packages for Ubuntu.

claim: dotnet-install.sh performs non-admin, side-by-side installs of specific SDK/runtime versions on Linux.
quote: The dotnet-install scripts are used to perform a non-admin installation of the .NET SDK, which includes the .NET CLI and the shared runtime.

claim: Bun ships native Linux builds with documented kernel requirements.
quote: Kernel version 5.6 or higher is recommended; Bun runs on kernels as old as 3.10 (RHEL 7) with graceful degradation of newer syscalls.

claim: DBeaver Community ships native Linux .deb, .rpm and zip packages.
quote: run sudo dpkg -i dbeaver-<version>.deb. Then execute dbeaver &.

claim: DB Browser for SQLite ships Linux AppImage, Snap and distro packages.
quote: Our latest release is available as an AppImage, Snap packages, and distribution specific packages:

claim: Beyond Compare 5.2.4 (July 2026) ships 64-bit Linux Debian and RPM packages.
quote: v5.2.4, build 32425, released July 22, 2026

claim: Every Beyond Compare licence sold since 2016 is multiplatform, so an existing BC5 key activates the Linux build.
quote: As of 2016, all Beyond Compare licenses sold are multiplatform. In addition to Windows support, we added Linux support in BC3 and macOS in BC4.

claim: Docker Desktop for Linux exists but runs the engine inside a VM with its own docker context, so it adds a layer that native Docker Engine does not have.
quote: Docker Desktop on Linux runs a Virtual Machine (VM) which creates and uses a custom docker context, `desktop-linux`, on startup.

claim: Podman is the free container-tooling alternative for managing containers, pods and images from a local Linux environment.
quote: Manage containers, pods, and images with Podman. Seamlessly work with containers and Kubernetes from your local environment.

claim: MSYS2 exists to provide a POSIX build environment for native Windows software, so it has no purpose on Linux.
quote: MSYS2 is a collection of tools and libraries providing you with an easy-to-use environment for building, installing and running native Windows software.

claim: C# Dev Kit is free for individuals, academic and open-source use and for commercial teams of up to 5; 6+ developers need a Visual Studio Professional subscription.
quote: For personal, academic, and open-source projects, C# Dev Kit can be used at no cost. For commercial purposes, teams of up to 5 can also use the C# Dev Kit at no cost.

claim: The C# Dev Kit licence bars Enterprises (>250 users/PCs or >$1M revenue) from using it for anything but open-source and education.
quote: If you are an Enterprise, your users may not use the Software to develop or test your applications, except for open source and education purposes.

claim: ReSharper 2026.2 for VS Code-compatible editors added debugging, value tracking and call/type hierarchy, and supports VS Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Devin Desktop and Kiro.
quote: the most requested feature is finally live: debugging

claim: ReSharper 2026.1 extended ReSharper beyond Visual Studio into VS Code and compatible editors with C#/XAML/Razor/Blazor analysis, solution-wide refactorings and unit testing.
quote: The extension provides: Gold-standard code analysis for C#, XAML, Razor, and Blazor

claim: Rider has no visual WPF/WinForms designers; for drag-and-drop layout designers Visual Studio remains the only serious option.
quote: Rider handles WPF code perfectly well, but there are no visual designers.

claim: EventPipe is the cross-platform replacement for ETW; from .NET 10 it can emit Linux user_events for unified managed+kernel traces, requiring root and kernel 6.4+.
quote: The goal of EventPipe is to allow .NET developers to easily trace their .NET applications without having to rely on platform-specific high-privilege components such as ETW or perf_events.

claim: dotnet-trace is a cross-platform CLI tool collecting .NET traces without a native profiler, built on EventPipe as the cross-platform alternative to ETW and LTTng.
quote: dotnet-trace is a cross-platform CLI global tool that enables the collection of .NET Core traces of a running process without any native profiler involved.

claim: SSMS requires 64-bit Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2016+ and .NET Framework 4.8; there is no Linux build.
quote: SSMS needs 64-bit Windows 10/11 (or Windows Server 2016+) and .NET Framework 4.8 or newer.

claim: SSMS 21 moved to the 64-bit Visual Studio 2022 shell and remains Windows-only.
quote: SSMS 21 is based on Visual Studio 2022 (64-bit), so it can use the new features integrated with Visual Studio.

claim: Rider bundles the Database Tools and SQL plugin by default, covering SQL Server versions 10-17.
quote: The Database Tools and SQL plugin is bundled and enabled in JetBrains Rider by default.

claim: Rider's database support is the DataGrip engine embedded in the IDE.
quote: Rider provides robust support for working with databases directly within the IDE – powered by DataGrip!

claim: Practitioner reading of the ADS retirement: SQL Server Agent and Profiler have no VS Code equivalent and ADS notebooks move to a different runtime.
quote: SQL Server Agent and Profiler are SSMS-only. If you managed Agent jobs or ran traces from ADS, those features have no VS Code equivalent.

claim: The MSSQL extension's Local SQL Server container wizard works on Linux, defaults to SQL Server 2025, is development-only, needs Docker running, and explicitly does not support Podman.
quote: No support for Podman.

claim: SQL Server Linux containers accept MSSQL_PID values EnterpriseDeveloper and StandardDeveloper, both free with no production use rights.
quote: Acceptable values: 1) Evaluation (free, no production use rights, 180-day limit) 2) EnterpriseDeveloper (free, no production use rights) 3) StandardDeveloper (free, no production use rights)

claim: SQL Server Developer edition is free for non-production development and test, and SQL Server 2025 splits it into Standard Developer and Enterprise Developer.
quote: SQL Server Developer is a full-featured, free edition licensed for use as a development and test database in non-production environments.

claim: SQL Server 2025 Linux containers on ARM/hybrid-CPU hosts remain an open unresolved issue.
quote: SQL Server 2025 on Linux with hybrid CPU architecture

claim: ARM64 support for SQL Server 2025 containers is still only a feature request.
quote: [Feature Request]: Add support for SQL Server 2025 containers on ARM architecture

claim: SQL Server 2025 RTM containers require AVX CPU instructions and crashed under emulation until CU1 fixed it.
quote: SQL Server 2025 RTM requires AVX (Advanced Vector Extensions) CPU instructions.

claim: Testcontainers for .NET spins up throwaway SQL Server containers per test run, replacing LocalDB in integration tests.
quote: A library to support tests with throwaway instances of Docker containers for all compatible .NET Standard versions.

claim: 2026 walkthrough of SQL Server integration testing with Testcontainers, each test class getting an isolated database.
quote: Testcontainers lets you run real SQL Server in Docker inside your tests.

claim: msodbcsql18 is the current Microsoft ODBC driver and installs on Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, SLES, Alpine and Azure Linux alongside unixODBC.
quote: Packages named msodbcsql18-* are the latest version of the Microsoft ODBC driver for SQL Server.

claim: The Microsoft OLE DB Driver for SQL Server is Windows-only; the current 19.4.2 release ships only Windows x64/Arm64/x86 installers.
quote: OLE DB Driver for SQL Server is available on Windows and delivers the SQL OLE DB driver in one dynamic-link library (DLL).

claim: Kestrel is the default cross-platform ASP.NET Core server and the default debug server, which makes IIS Express redundant.
quote: Kestrel is the default, recommended cross-platform web server and is also the default debug server in Visual Studio for ASP.NET Core projects.

claim: Microsoft's documented Linux hosting model is Kestrel run as a systemd unit behind an nginx reverse proxy.
quote: Configure a reverse proxy server to forward requests to the Kestrel web server.

claim: Caddy is a single-binary multi-platform web server with automatic HTTPS, a lighter reverse proxy in front of Kestrel than nginx.
quote: Fast and extensible multi-platform HTTP/1-2-3 web server with automatic HTTPS

claim: Web Deploy is an MSI-installed Windows/IIS technology depending on the Web Management Service, SMO and IIS Manager.
quote: Using the Web Deploy Installer, Web Deploy can be installed on Windows 2012 Server or later, or Windows 8.0 or later.

claim: Trusting the ASP.NET Core dev certificate on Linux needs manual system-CA and NSS-store work; DOTNET_DEV_CERTS_NSSDB_PATHS points at extra NSS databases.
quote: You can use the DOTNET_DEV_CERTS_NSSDB_PATHS environment variable to specify a colon-delimited list of NSS directories

claim: linux-dev-certs is a community dotnet tool that creates a CA-signed dev certificate trusted by the system store and by Firefox where browsers ignore system certs.
quote: Because the tool uses a CA-signed development certificate, the local HTTPS endpoint is trusted by a broader part of the system (browsers, tools, ...).

claim: Zeal is a cross-platform offline documentation browser, the practical stand-in for Help Viewer's offline library.
quote: Zeal is an offline documentation browser for software developers.

claim: Zeal is actively developed and uses Dash-format docsets.
quote: Offline documentation browser. Your personal reference library, searchable in an instant.

claim: Visual Studio Tools for Applications 2019 is a Windows-only redistributable, normally pulled in by a third-party application rather than chosen.
quote: Microsoft Visual Studio Tools for Applications 2019

claim: VSTA is an ISV customization/extensibility toolkit tied to .NET Framework.
quote: Visual Studio Tools for Applications (VSTA) is a set of tools that independent software vendors (ISVs) can use to build customization abilities into their applications.

claim: ILSpy v11's Avalonia UI builds on Linux and macOS, but as of June 2026 prebuilt binaries exist only for Windows, so Linux users must compile it themselves.
quote: prebuilt binaries only exist for Windows at the moment. If you want to give the current bits a try on Mac and Linux, please see...on how to build it yourself.

claim: AvaloniaILSpy is archived and unmaintained; the project points cross-platform users at the ILSpy VS Code extension.
quote: we recommend using ilspy-vscode, which has more features than AvaloniaILSpy and is available on all platforms thanks to VS Code

claim: ilspy-vscode runs the ILSpy decompiler inside VS Code on every platform via a C# backend service.
quote: ILSpy Visual Studio Code Extension and Service for Decompiling .NET Assemblies

claim: Rider's Assembly Explorer is a cross-platform .NET decompiler based on the dotPeek engine, working on Windows, macOS and Linux.
quote: Rider's assembly explorer is a cross-platform .NET decompiler that works on Windows, Mac OS X and Linux, based on dotPeek.

claim: WPF only runs on Windows even though .NET itself is cross-platform, and its XAML designer requires Visual Studio.
quote: Even though .NET is a cross-platform technology, WPF only runs on Windows.

claim: Avalonia XPF is a commercial binary-compatibility layer that runs unmodified WPF apps on desktop Linux, including third-party control suites.
quote: Avalonia XPF enables you to run your existing WPF app on macOS and Linux without modification.

claim: Avalonia is the mainstream open-source XAML UI framework for cross-platform .NET desktop apps.
quote: Develop Desktop, Embedded, Mobile and WebAssembly apps with C# and XAML. The future of .NET UI

claim: Uno Platform is the other cross-platform XAML option, single-codebase across desktop, web, mobile and embedded.
quote: Open-source platform for building cross-platform native Mobile, Web, Desktop, and Embedded apps from a single C#/XAML codebase.

claim: SqlPackage is a cross-platform CLI installable as a dotnet tool on Linux for dacpac/bacpac publish, extract and export.
quote: SqlPackage is a command-line utility for database portability and deployments in Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.

claim: SqlPackage 170.4 (June 2026) can reverse-engineer a live database straight into a Microsoft.Build.Sql SQL project, the cross-platform successor to classic SSDT .sqlproj.
quote: Set the ExtractTarget property to SqlProject during extract to reverse engineer the database into a Microsoft.Build.Sql project instead of the default .dacpac output format.

claim: The rewritten sqlcmd is a Go CLI shipped for Linux via .deb/.rpm/tar and Linuxbrew.
quote: The new sqlcmd, CLI for SQL Server and Azure SQL

claim: mise manages dev tools, env vars and tasks per project from one CLI.
quote: One tool that manages dev tools, env vars, and tasks per project.

claim: mise is a Rust tool-version manager with broad 2026 adoption.
quote: dev tools, env vars, task runner

claim: nvm-sh/nvm is the POSIX-shell Node version manager that NVM for Windows imitates, and the direct Linux equivalent.
quote: Node Version Manager - POSIX-compliant bash script to manage multiple active node.js versions

claim: fnm is a fast Rust Node version manager, a drop-in for nvm on Linux.
quote: Fast and simple Node.js version manager, built in Rust

claim: rbenv plus ruby-build is the standard Linux replacement for RubyInstaller's managed Ruby.
quote: Manage your app's Ruby environment

claim: uv installs and pins CPython versions and manages projects, covering what python.org installers plus the py launcher did on Windows.
quote: An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.

claim: uv is the dominant 2026 Python toolchain manager by adoption.
quote: An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.

claim: pyenv remains the conservative choice for multiple Python versions on Linux.
quote: Simple Python version management

claim: Robo 3T is effectively abandoned after the Studio 3T acquisition; last release 1.4.4, no fixes and no compatibility work for newer MongoDB versions; Compass runs on Linux.
quote: Robo 3T still launches and connects to many existing deployments, but gets no new features, no fixes, and no compatibility work for newer MongoDB versions.

claim: MongoDB Compass is the free official MongoDB GUI.
quote: MongoDB Compass: The free GUI tool for data exploration.

claim: HeidiSQL now publishes native Linux builds (Debian and RPM, Qt6/Qt5/GTK2 variants plus ARM64), current stable v12.20 from 2026-06-22.
quote: Linux x64 Debian package with QT6 build

claim: The HeidiSQL author states Wine is unstable and the native Linux build is the alternative, still in beta.
quote: Running HeidiSQL on Wine is currently quite unstable.

claim: Rider 2026.2 (July 2026) adds WPF Hot Reload, more reliable source-generator debugging on Linux and macOS, and native GitHub Copilot agent integration.
quote: more reliable source generator debugging on Linux and macOS

claim: dotMemory integrated in Rider on Linux is functionally identical to the standalone Windows tool, and a Linux command-line profiler exists.
quote: dotMemory integrated in JetBrains Rider for Windows, macOS, and Linux. In terms of functionality, the integrated version is identical to the standalone one.

claim: dotUltimate bundles Rider, ReSharper and the dot* tools in one paid subscription, listed around $597 for a first-year commercial seat in mid-2026.
quote: dotUltimate includes all .NET tools, ReSharper C++, and JetBrains Rider together in one pack.

claim: A community .NET Standard reimplementation of Microsoft.SqlServer.Types covers client-side geometry/geography/hierarchyid on Linux.
quote: a .NET Standard implementation of the spatial types in `Microsoft.SqlServer.Types`

claim: The MSSQL extension for VS Code provides Object Explorer, Table/Schema Designer, Schema Compare, Query Profiler, backup/restore, flat-file import and DACPAC/BACPAC operations cross-platform.
quote: The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code includes schema management, query execution, AI-powered assistance, and integrations for source control and CI/CD workflows.

claim: WPF is a framework for building Windows desktop applications, so the Windows Desktop Runtime has no Linux counterpart.
quote: WPF is a .NET Core UI framework for building Windows desktop applications.

claim: Windows Forms is likewise a Windows-only .NET UI stack.
quote: Windows Forms is a .NET UI framework for building Windows desktop applications.

claim: mise reads .nvmrc and other existing version files directly, so nvm/rbenv/pyenv projects work without conversion.
quote: Mise maintains backward compatibility with existing version files from nvm, rbenv, pyenv, and asdf.

claim: The request to make MSDeploy cross-platform was opened in 2016 and the repository was archived in 2020 with no cross-platform MSDeploy delivered.
quote: Make a new version of MSDeploy that is CrossPlat

claim: Podman is rootless by default and daemonless, while Docker requires explicit configuration for rootless operation.
quote: rootless Podman "just works" out-of-the-box, whereas Docker admins must explicitly enable and configure rootless operation
